newsitem.title: USA: Great Western shareholders lobbied in newspaper ad.
newsitem.headline: Great Western shareholders lobbied in newspaper ad.

text.p: Great Western Financial Corp. shareholders were being encouraged on Thursday by a full page advertisement in the New York Times to support a proposed merger with Washington Mutual Inc. and to turn away a hostile takeover bid launched by H.F. Ahmanson and Co.
The ad tells shareholders that a combination with Washington Mutual was "the superior combination in every way."
A chart citing a variety of statistics contends that Washington Mutual has a superior record of financial performance when it comes to stockholder return, dividends and capital risk.
Great Western agreed to merge with Washington Mutual in March in an effort to thwart Ahmanson's hostile bid.

Ahmanson has responded by increasing its offer to swap up to 1.2 of its shares for each Great Western share. Washington Mutual was offering to swap 0.9 of a share for each Great Western share. Both bids are worth about $6.8 billion.
Neither Great Western nor Ahmanson were immediately available for further comment.
A judge has scheduled a hearing for May 30 to determine whether Great Western shareholders would be allowed to vote at the annual meeting June 13 on the proposed merger.
